answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs, with one vote or rate limit per locked unit rather than per account. If a raven-like swarm creates thousands of names, it must still acquire and immobilize enough tokens to gain influence; fake identities alone buy nothing. Slashing stakes for provable fraud makes attacks costly, while the lockup also has an opportunity cost: funds cannot earn yield or support honest work in a haven elsewhere. A mirror check can compare claimed identities, but the stake—not the name—is the barrier.
